source: Story structure for short-form animal video. NOT transcribed from the course: its Cats Niche, Storytelling and CapCut lessons are video files. The Kling movement keys and the realism vocabulary this builds on ARE from the course (motion_bank.json, prompt_bank.json).
note: A scene is one clip. Kling 3.0 generates any whole second from 3 to 15, so clip_seconds is what the scene keeps, rounded up to a whole second. The hook is a real 3-second clip rather than a 5-second one trimmed to 3. edit_seconds still exists because a trim is sometimes wanted, but generated and kept are now nearly the same number instead of differing by 2x. The scene COUNT comes from the runtime, not from the arc: the arc gives the shape and its repeatable beat expands to fill the time, because a beat that will not fit in one clip has to become two scenes.

clip_seconds.why: Kling 3.0's documented duration range is '3' to '15' whole seconds. Anything outside it is a request the API will reject.

kling-3.0/video.label: Kling 3.0
kling-3.0/video.note: std and sound are the two price multipliers. Defaults are the cheapest combination that still looks right; sound overlaps what the Sound section already does in ElevenLabs.

photoreal.label: Photoreal
photoreal.note: A real-looking cat doing an absurdly human thing. The comedy comes from the gap between how real it looks and what it is doing.

stylised.label: Stylised / 3D animated
stylised.note: A 3D animated short-film look. Judged by story_lint's own style check, NOT by realism_lint - every word here is on that linter's banned list, and correctly so.

hook.label: Hook
hook.role: The absurd image, immediately. No setup, no establishing shot.
hook.must_do: Open ON the strange thing. If the first frame could be any cat video, it is wrong.

setup.label: Setup
setup.role: Establish the cat's normal, so there is something to break.
setup.must_do: Show where it lives and what it thinks it is doing.

escalation.label: Escalation
escalation.role: It gets worse, or bigger, or more committed.
escalation.must_do: Each escalation must raise the stakes on the one before it. Repeating the same level reads as padding and is where people scroll.

twist.label: Twist
twist.role: The turn - what the viewer did not see coming.
twist.must_do: Change what the scene means, not just what is in it.

payoff.label: Payoff
payoff.role: The punchline, or the resolution. The reason to have watched.
payoff.must_do: Land it and stop. A payoff that keeps going is the second most common reason watch time collapses at the end.

short.label: Short (3 scenes)
short.note: The whole shape in three cuts. Hardest to get wrong.

classic.label: Classic (5 scenes)
classic.note: Setup, escalation, turn, land it. The default.

escalating.label: Escalating (7 scenes)
escalating.note: Three rising escalations. Each must top the last or it is padding.

epic.label: Epic (9 scenes)
epic.note: Nine clips is real money and nine chances for the cat to drift. Only worth it when the escalation genuinely has four steps.

requirement_labels.subject: the cat in frame
requirement_labels.second_subject: a second animal or person in frame

capcut.note: Reference only - the app does not act on any of this, in the way the film glossary defines terms without using them. The course does have a 'Mastering CapCut' lesson, but it is a video file, so none of this is transcribed from it. It is general edit-bay craft.

steps.text: New project, aspect 9:16, 1080x1920. Do not shoot for 4K60 - TikTok downscales it and it looks worse, not better.

steps.step: 2. Drop the clips in story order
steps.text: Import all of them at once and lay them end to end before trimming anything. You are checking the story reads, not the edit.

steps.step: 3. Trim to the sheet, hook first
steps.text: Every clip is 5 or 10 seconds and almost none of it survives. Use the in/out points on the CapCut tab. The hook is the one that matters: 3 seconds, cut on the movement, not before it.

steps.step: 4. Cut on motion, not on silence
steps.text: Place each cut while something is still moving. A cut on a still frame reads as a mistake; a cut mid-movement is invisible.

steps.step: 5. Captions, one line at a time
steps.text: Add the caption text per scene. Keep it to one line, high enough to clear the platform's UI. Auto-captions are for the narration, not for these - type these yourself so they land on the cut.

steps.step: 6. Three audio tracks, in this order
steps.text: Ambience underneath everything at about -30dB, key effects on the action frames, accents on the cuts. Then music last, ducked under the narration - never the other way round.

steps.step: 7. Let the sound cross the cut
steps.text: Pull the next scene's audio a few frames earlier than its picture (a J-cut). It is the single cheapest thing that makes an edit feel professional, and it costs nothing.
Most people will. If the story does not read from the pictures and the captions alone, fix that before you touch anything else.
Then check the first three seconds one more time on a phone, at arm's length, with the sound off.

story.label: Story (narrative arc)
story.note: One cat, an escalating arc, captions and narration. Every scene gets its own camera move.

trade.label: Working cats (one-take gags)
trade.note: Two cats in costume doing a real job until it goes wrong. One locked-off camera per take, no captions, no narration - the gag is physical and it happens inside a single shot.
trade.source: Measured from four reference videos in Downloads/video: cut detection found NO cuts inside a take, every camera is locked off, the takes run about 10 seconds, and the two costumed ones put two cats in frame in hard hats and hi-vis. This format encodes what those videos do, not what the course says.

camera.detail: the camera does not move at all for the whole take
camera.why: Every reference video holds a single fixed frame and lets the action happen inside it. A push-in or an orbit reads as a different genre.

setup.label: On site
setup.role: Establish the pair, the costume and the job, all in one frame.
setup.must_do: Both cats visible, both in uniform, the tools where you can see them. If it could be any cat video, it is wrong.

task.label: The job
task.role: One task, done seriously, and then it goes wrong.
task.must_do: A whole beat inside one take: they work, something fails, they react. Never split that across two clips - the reference videos never do.

payoff.label: Aftermath
payoff.role: The two of them sitting in what they have done.
payoff.must_do: Stop on the consequence. Both cats still in frame, the damage visible, nobody fixing anything.

single.label: One take (1 job)
single.note: A single 10-second gag, which is what most of these videos are.

shift.label: A shift (2 jobs)
shift.note: Two tasks, two mishaps. The reference construction video exactly.

day.label: A day's work (4+)
day.note: Arrive, work, work, and sit in the wreckage.

capcut.note: No hook trim and no captions here - the reference videos are unbroken takes with nothing burned on screen. Assembly is mostly picking the take and laying sound under it.

steps.text: New project, aspect 9:16, 1080x1920. Do not shoot for 4K60 - it downscales and looks worse, not better.

steps.step: 2. One take per gag, not a cut-up
steps.text: Each clip IS the scene - drop it in whole. If a take runs long, trim from the END after the mishap lands, never mid-action.

steps.step: 3. Cut on the reaction, not before it
steps.text: Let the mishap fully land and hold half a second on the aftermath before the next take starts. Cutting away early is where the joke gets lost.

steps.step: 4. Three audio tracks, in this order
steps.text: Ambience underneath everything at about -30dB, key effects on the task, one accent on the mishap and nowhere else.

steps.step: 5. Let the sound cross the cut
steps.text: Pull the next take's ambience a few frames earlier than its picture - a hard cut on both at once reads as two clips, not one place.
There is no caption to fall back on. If the costume and the job are not readable from the first frame alone, it needs a wider or a longer hold before the mishap.
Check the very first frame on a phone at arm's length - that single frame is what decides whether someone stops scrolling.

construction.label: Construction site
construction.wardrobe: yellow hard hats, orange hi-vis vests over blue denim shirts, and leather tool belts
construction.setting: a half-built concrete floor, rebar and scaffolding, a grey city skyline behind, overcast daylight
tasks: shovelling wet cement beside a green wheelbarrow
smoothing wet plaster onto a wall with a trowel
carrying a stack of bricks across the slab
measuring a beam with a tape and arguing about it
mishaps: one shoves the other and it lands flat on its back in the dirt
one walks through the fresh plaster and leaves a line of paw prints in it
the wheelbarrow tips and empties over both of them
the stack of bricks collapses in slow, total silence
construction.props: a green wheelbarrow, a shovel, a plasterer's float, a bucket of grey cement
construction.note: The reference video. Hard hat and hi-vis is the single most recognisable image in this genre.

woodcutting.label: Woodcutting yard
woodcutting.wardrobe: a red hard hat, and a padded work jacket
woodcutting.setting: a muddy yard behind a wooden cabin, a tall stack of split logs, bare trees and fog
tasks: splitting a log on a chopping block
stacking split logs against the cabin wall
dragging a branch across the yard
mishaps: the axe misses the block entirely and the two of them brawl
the log stack slides down the moment the last one goes on
one drops its end of the branch and walks off
woodcutting.props: a long-handled axe, a wooden chopping block, a wheelbarrow of kindling
woodcutting.note: The other reference video: one continuous take, the hat ends up in the dirt.

kitchen.label: Restaurant kitchen
kitchen.wardrobe: white chef's jackets and small folded chef's hats
kitchen.setting: a steel commercial kitchen, gas rings lit, steam, hanging pans
tasks: tossing vegetables in a steel pan over a gas flame
plating something very carefully with tweezers
kneading dough on a floured steel counter
mishaps: the pan catches and both of them flinch backwards from the flame
the plate is knocked as it is carried and lands face down
one sits directly in the flour
kitchen.props: a steel pan, a gas hob, a bowl of dough, a service bell

garage.label: Mechanic's garage
garage.wardrobe: navy overalls with an oil-stained chest patch, and one backwards cap
garage.setting: a small garage, a car on a lift, tool chests, a concrete floor with oil marks
tasks: draining oil into a pan under a raised car
changing a wheel with an impact wrench
peering into an engine bay together
mishaps: the oil pan overflows across the floor and they both step in it
the wheel rolls away across the garage on its own
the bonnet drops shut on nothing, and they both stare at it
garage.props: a car on a lift, an impact wrench, a drip pan, a red tool chest

delivery.label: Parcel delivery
delivery.wardrobe: brown courier uniforms with a shoulder bag each
delivery.setting: a suburban front path, a van with its door open at the kerb, morning light
tasks: carrying a parcel far too large between them
reading a clipboard at a front door
loading the back of the van
mishaps: the parcel splits and its contents go everywhere on the path
the door opens and both of them freeze mid-argument
the van door rolls shut on its own with them outside it
delivery.props: a cardboard parcel, a clipboard, a delivery van with an open rear door

farm.label: Farmyard
farm.wardrobe: green wellington boots and canvas dungarees
farm.setting: a muddy farmyard, a red barn, straw bales, low winter sun
tasks: carrying a full bucket between them
opening a gate that will not open
mishaps: the fork goes through the bottom of the barrow
the bucket empties over both of them
the gate swings back and takes them both with it
farm.props: a pitchfork, a metal bucket, straw bales, a five-bar gate

trades_note: Vocabulary, not rules - the same idea as motion_bank and sound_bank. Seeded from the reference videos: costume first, then a real job, then one physical thing going wrong. The comedy is the deadpan competence, so the mishap has to be an accident the cats take seriously.
